name: Pudendal Nerve Entrapment Syndrome

criteria.description: Pain in the anatomical territory of the pudendal nerve (perineum, genitalia, anus)
Pain is predominantly experienced while sitting and relieved by standing or sitting on a toilet seat
Sensory abnormalities in the pudendal nerve distribution such as numbness or dysesthesia
Exclusion of other causes of pelvic pain by imaging and clinical evaluation
Temporary pain relief following pudendal nerve block

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all major criteria including pain in pudendal nerve territory, pain worsened by sitting, exclusion of other causes, with supportive findings such as nerve block response
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and nerve block tests; electrophysiological studies may assist but are not definitive.

imaging: MRI pelvis to exclude other causes and visualize pudendal nerve entrapment
CT or ultrasound-guided pudendal nerve block for diagnostic confirmation
other: Electrophysiological studies (pudendal nerve terminal motor latency test) may show delayed conduction
Clinical response to pudendal nerve block

distinguishingFeatures: Pain not localized to pudendal nerve distribution
Lack of pain relief with pudendal nerve block
Pain worsened by specific joint maneuvers rather than sitting

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe perineal pain with neurological deficits
Progressive urinary retention or fecal incontinence
Signs of infection or malignancy in pelvic region
references: Labat JJ, Riant T, Robert R, et al. Diagnostic criteria for pudendal neuralgia by pudendal nerve entrapment (Nantes criteria). Neurourol Urodyn. 2008;27(4):306-310.
Shafik A. Pudendal nerve entrapment syndrome: a cause of chronic pelvic pain. J Urol. 1991;146(6):1619-1622.
Robert R, Riant T, Labat JJ. Pudendal neuralgia: clinical features and surgical treatment. Prog Urol. 2005;15(3): 330-335.
